name: Calabresella
description: Calabresella (also known as Terziglio) is an Italian three-player point-trick game with bidding. It is closely related to Tressette. The main aim is to capture aces and take the last trick, which is difficult because there are no trumps. The game features an unusual card order with threes as the highest cards.

content.text: Calabresella (also known as Terziglio) is an Italian three-player point-trick game with bidding. It is closely related to Tressette. The main aim is to capture aces and take the last trick, which is difficult because there are no trumps. The game features an unusual card order with threes as the highest cards.

Country/Region of Origin: Italy
Time Period: Traditional game, documented since 19th century
Historical Development: Related to Tressette and other Italian point-trick games. An American variation was described in 1870 by Cavendish (Henry Jones). The name Calabresella suggests origins in Calabria region.
Cultural Significance: Played throughout Italy, particularly popular in traditional card-playing circles.

Minimum Players: 3
Maximum Players: 4 (dealer sits out)
Optimal Players: 3
Partnerships: No

Type: 40-card Italian or French suited pack
Card Ranks: 3 (high), 2, Ace, King, Queen (or Horse), Jack, 7, 6, 5, 4 (low)
Suits: Swords, Batons, Cups, Coins (Italian) or Spades, Clubs, Hearts, Diamonds (French)

40-card Italian or French pack
Score sheet
Table space

Cards per Player: 13 cards each (3 players), dealer receives 14 and discards one
Dealing Pattern: Anticlockwise
Discard: Dealer discards one card to the winner of the last trick
